target: cETH accrued-interest payouts to balance-holding accounts (AccrueDistributed recipients): holder-side payout stream
why: Non-liquidation payout class per decisions/human/2026-11-08-beyond-liquidations.md, split off from lead 79's dead_end (attempts 529, 2026-11-08 run 799d0dfe). The AccrueDistributed payouts measured in the class go to accounts holding SMALL cETH balances whose balances stay unchanged after the payout: recipient 0x60b0f1919cf4ee46d1a8d63428276512814de570 held 107,110,539 cETH tokens (~1.07 cETH, ~0.0214 ETH value) at tag 26365771 and received 0.021534003934147722 ETH in tx 0x92a8bce (block 26365772); recipient 0x8f10b468b06c6fd214b65f87778827f7d113f996 received 0.00907119364274966 ETH in tx 0x6fcdf3e82e3b598c... (block 26365190) - both mantissa 45117721. A zero-balance dust redeemer pays 0-9 wei (measured), so the payout looks proportional to holding a cETH position: a bot holding ~50 USD of cETH could test whether it captures the same stream. Pool thin: only 2 non-zero-payout txs in blocks 26348613-26368613 (4 d, 20000 blocks, wiki mechanisms/compound-accrue-interest-to-caller.md addendum 2) = ~0.5 events/day at 20-48 USD gross, while the 7d census saw big payments >= 0.5 USD at 3.1/day avg 8.6 USD (different windows, conflict noted on both). No incumbent known for the holder side.
next_steps: Measure before any build: (1) ledger query compound_v2.accrue_distributed for the last 30 d: recipient addresses, payout sizes, and how often the SAME recipient is paid repeatedly (holder stream cadence); (2) for one recipient, read cETH balanceOf at its payout blocks (relay historical tag) and check balance decay vs payout - is the payout free on top of the balance or an exchange-rate-funded redemption?; (3) only if payouts recur on held balances: size a bot minting ~50 USD cETH once (cETH mint needs ETH deposit; measure the mint/redeem gas) and re-measure EV after gas (134k gas x measured basefee). CETH exchange rate ~0.02 ETH per cETH unit (1.07 cETH ~ 0.0214 ETH payout match, measured 2026-11-08).
